title: The Atlas of Port Mahon
premise: In 1799, on the British-occupied island of Menorca, apprentice mapmaker Lior Thornbury secretly completes the atlas her dead master died protecting—an atlas whose coastal charts could decide who holds Port Mahon. When a stranger arrives bearing letters in the master's unmistakable hand, Lior learns he may be alive and that the finished atlas is both ransom and proof. To save him and herself, she must smuggle the evidence past three military checkpoints before the century turns, choosing between duty to the Crown that employs her and love for a man the empire declared dead.
about_author: Ulyana Okonkwo is a former cartographer's assistant turned novelist who grew up between Lagos and Lisbon, harbors of stories. She writes historical fiction about people whose careful hands hold dangerous things.

chapters.title: The Ink That Outlived Him
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the drafty Port Mahon workshop, Lior inks the final plates of Master Aldous Renwick's atlas, officially listed as drowned two years prior. She hides her grief in precision until a storm-battered stranger, Callum Vey, arrives with letters written in Renwick's living hand. Emotional beat: shock cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: What the Charts Betray
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He reveals Renwick faked his death to keep the atlas from both Crowns, and that its soundings expose a route the Navy will weaponize. The garrison commander, Major Hesse, has begun asking questions at the workshop door. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged under threat.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Disguising the atlas plates inside a coffin shipment of survey instruments, Lior talks her way past a suspicious clerk who knew Renwick personally. She succeeds, but Hesse notes her name in his ledger. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into audacity; first blood drawn in the game.

chapters.title: Letters to a Ghost
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, interwoven with Renwick's letters read aloud. Through Callum's recitation, Lior falls further for a man she knows only through ink—while Callum watches her fall and says nothing of his own quiet devotion. Emotional beat: love against duty sharpening into an impossible triangle.

chapters.title: Hesse's Invitation
chapters.summary: Major Hesse's POV. The commander summons Lior to dinner, flattering her skill while displaying a confiscated fragment of Renwick's correspondence. He offers protection in exchange for the atlas, making clear refusal means the gallows. Emotional beat: the trap closing; duty wearing a charming face.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint: San Felipe Road
chapters.summary: Lior and Callum's alternating POV. They move the plates by mule cart through the hill fort road as a search party sweeps behind them; Callum takes a soldier's bullet graze covering their escape. In a cave, feverish, he confesses Renwick sent him not to rescue the atlas but to destroy it. Emotional beat: betrayal within trust.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Mapmaker
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone with the plates, Lior weighs three futures: surrender the atlas to Hesse, burn it as Renwick asked, or finish it and let the truth sail free. She chooses a fourth path—alter the charts so they protect the harbor rather than betray it. Emotional beat: agency seized; grief becoming craft.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint: The Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: Climax. On New Year's Eve, Lior walks the plates through the harbor gate beneath fireworks while Hesse waits with arrest orders—and Renwick himself steps from the crowd, alive, to take her place in the line of fire. Callum turns the crowd's festival chaos against the soldiers. Emotional beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Renwick's POV. At midnight, aboard a departing brig, Renwick explains why he stayed dead: the atlas was never meant to be saved, but corrected. He sees what Lior has done to his charts and names her master of the work, not apprentice. Emotional beat: recognition; the debt of love acknowledged without possession.

chapters.title: A New Projection
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, one year later. From a small studio above the harbor, Lior publishes the corrected atlas under her own name, sending Renwick's original letters to his family and keeping only one—for herself. Callum returns with news of safe harbors elsewhere; she chooses to stay, and asks him to stay too. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, memory honored, love answered.
